items.headline: FAA blames ground stop on equipment issue
items.summary: The FAA said Friday's nationwide ground stop was caused by an equipment issue during a contractor's telecommunications upgrade at a remote site. Airlines canceled thousands of flights Saturday as they worked to recover, and questions grew about the age of the air traffic control system.

items.headline: Zelenskyy warns U.S. security plan could aid Putin
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a new European security framework floated by the U.S. could benefit Vladimir Putin. European leaders insisted that Europeans must decide their own security.

items.headline: Trump's shifting Iran rhetoric leaves region in limbo
items.summary: President Trump's changing comments on Iran since the U.S. elections have left uncertainty about the next steps in the conflict. U.S. allies are struggling with its economic effects.

items.headline: Alaska elects Democratic governor, keeps ranked-choice voting
items.summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the race for Alaska governor, the first Democrat elected to the office since 1998, giving Democrats 30 governorships. Alaska voters also rejected a second attempt to repeal ranked-choice voting and the top-four primary.

items.headline: Starship caught by launch pad arms after orbit
items.summary: SpaceX's Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the launch pad's arms for the first time. The booster failed after liftoff, so the planned double catch did not happen.

items.headline: Microsoft restores services after global outage
items.summary: Microsoft said its services were fully restored after a global outage. The disruption had affected governments, courts, health care, airlines and banks in many countries.

items.headline: States get six more months on Medicaid work rules
items.summary: The administration gave states six more months, until July 1, before they must remove people from Medicaid for not meeting work requirements. The extension delays a key part of the new rules.

items.headline: Fuel crisis and protests pressure Chile's president
items.summary: Rising fuel prices have set off transport strikes and protests across Chile. The unrest is increasing pressure on the country's far-right president.

items.headline: Democrats weigh lessons of failed Hegseth impeachment
items.summary: The failed impeachment of Pete Hegseth has become a test for Democrats as they prepare to hold House and Senate majorities. An NPR analysis says they face hard choices on priorities, timing and messaging.

items.headline: New organ donation policy draws ethics debate
items.summary: New organ-retrieval guidelines are meant to help ease the U.S. organ shortage while protecting donors. Bioethicists question whether the procedure is ethical.

digest.overview:
Airlines expected to cancel 4,000 to 5,000 of roughly 41,000 scheduled U.S. flights Sunday as air travel recovers from Friday's nationwide ground stop, which the FAA blamed on an equipment issue during a contractor's telecommunications upgrade. Microsoft said its services were fully restored after a global outage that disrupted governments, courts, hospitals, airlines and banks. SpaceX caught a returning Starship with its launch pad arms for the first time after a mission of more than 22 hours. Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won Alaska's governorship, his party's first there since 1998, as voters again refused to repeal ranked-choice voting and Democrat Mary Peltola widened her lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan. The administration gave states until July 1 before removing people from Medicaid under work requirements. The CDC said seven states had high flu activity last week, an unusually early start.

Abroad, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that a European security framework floated by the U.S. could benefit Vladimir Putin, while the Kremlin said Putin, Xi Jinping and President Trump will meet Nov. 19 in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz, and claimed to have shot down a U.S. MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island. Türkiye and 17 other countries condemned an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis. Chile's president faces mounting protests and transport strikes over rising fuel prices. Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million for accessing Android users' photos and data without informed consent.

home.overview:
Miami kept rolling with a fourth straight win, 137–117 over Detroit, as Giannis Antetokounmpo put up 34 points, 14 rebounds and 8 assists and Klay Thompson hit six 3s. Cleveland beat Dallas 127–117 with all five starters resting thanks to a Tyrese Proctor triple-double, Denver sent New Orleans to a sixth straight loss, and Chicago snapped Minnesota's five-game streak. Sunday's nine NBA games include Lakers-Suns and Mavericks-Celtics. NFL Week 10 opens with Patriots-Lions in Munich at 9:30 a.m. ET, but Kansas City will reportedly be without league-leading rusher Kenneth Walker III, and backup referees will work several games after Friday's FAA ground stop. Steelers-Bengals closes Sunday night. In baseball, four clubs have shown interest in Dustin May, and qualifying-offer decisions are due Tuesday.

The USMNT routed Haiti 6–0 in Miami behind two goals from Christian Pulisic in the first leg of its Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal. Denmark thrashed Portugal 4–1 in Braga in their first game since Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement, and Japan stunned Brazil 3–2 in Singapore as Carlo Ancelotti and Raphinha were sent off. Spain host England tonight, Germany and the Netherlands meet Monday in Berlin, and club play returns next weekend. In baseball, South Korea beat Taiwan 6–4 to reach Sunday's Asia Professional Baseball Championship final against Japan.

brief: South Korea beat Taiwan 6–4 at Tokyo Dome on Saturday to reach the Asia Professional Baseball Championship final, with Kim Do-yeong's tiebreaking solo homer in the fifth one of three Korean solo shots.
Korea, which had lost to Australia and Japan, advanced on the Team Quality Balance tiebreaker after Japan beat Australia 16–1 to finish the round robin 3–0.
Korea face Japan in Sunday night's final at Tokyo Dome, the countries' third straight APBC final meeting; Japan won the previous two.
Back home, KBO free-agent negotiations open Tuesday, Nov. 17, with Samsung's Koo Ja-wook and Won Tae-in heading the list.
